{{Short description|Theory of gravity}}
{{refimprove|date=October 2020}}

{{confuse|Gauss–Bonnet theorem}}
In [[general relativity]], '''Gauss–Bonnet gravity''', also referred to as '''Einstein–Gauss–Bonnet gravity''',<ref>{{Citation | last = Lovelock | first = David | title = The Einstein tensor and its generalizations | journal = J. Math. Phys. | volume = 12 | issue = 3 | pages = 498–501 | year = 1971 | doi=10.1063/1.1665613|bibcode = 1971JMP....12..498L | doi-access = free }}</ref> is a modification of the [[Einstein–Hilbert action]] to include the [[generalized Gauss–Bonnet theorem|Gauss–Bonnet term]]<ref>{{Cite book|last=Roos|first=Matts|url=https://www.wiley.com/en-us/Introduction+to+Cosmology%2C+4th+Edition-p-9781118923320|title=Introduction to Cosmology|publisher=Wiley|year=2015|edition=4th|pages=248}}</ref> (named after [[Carl Friedrich Gauss]] and [[Pierre Ossian Bonnet]]) 

:<math>\int d^Dx \sqrt{-g}\, G</math>,

where

:<math>G= R^2 - 4R^{\mu\nu}R_{\mu\nu} + R^{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}R_{\mu\nu\rho\sigma} </math>.

This term is only nontrivial in 4+1D or greater, and as such, only applies to extra dimensional models. In 3+1D, it reduces to a topological [[divergence theorem|surface term]]. This follows from the [[generalized Gauss–Bonnet theorem]] on a 4D manifold

:<math>\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int d^4x \sqrt{-g}\, G = \chi(M)</math>.

In lower dimensions, it identically vanishes.

Despite being quadratic in the [[Riemann tensor]] (and [[Ricci tensor]]), terms containing more than 2 partial derivatives of the [[metric tensor|metric]] cancel out, making the [[Euler–Lagrange equations]] [[partial differential equation#Linear equations of second order|second order]] [[Differential equation|quasilinear]] [[partial differential equations]] in the metric. Consequently, there are no additional dynamical degrees of freedom, as in say [[f(R) gravity]].

Gauss–Bonnet gravity has also been shown to be connected to [[Covariant formulation of classical electromagnetism|classical electrodynamics]] by means of complete gauge invariance with respect to [[Noether's theorem]].<ref>{{Citation  |author1=Baker, Mark Robert |author2=Kuzmin, Sergei | title = A connection between linearized Gauss–Bonnet gravity and classical electrodynamics | journal = Int. J. Mod. Phys. D | volume = 28 | issue = 7 |pages=1950092–22 | year = 2019 | doi=10.1142/S0218271819500925| arxiv = 1811.00394 |bibcode=2019IJMPD..2850092B }}</ref>

More generally, we may consider a
:<math>\int d^Dx \sqrt{-g}\, f\left( G \right)</math>
term for some function ''f''. Nonlinearities in ''f'' render this coupling nontrivial even in 3+1D. Therefore, fourth order terms reappear with the nonlinearities.
